notes: 8 configurations / 8 equipment entries from 6 manufacturers (RETSCH, ZwickRoell, Qualitest x3, Tinius Olsen, Cryogenics International, Cole-Parmer SamplePrep/SPEX), all accessed 2026-11-01; none duplicates data/cryostats (the existing RETSCH CryoMill/MM 400 and Messer cabinet are different machines) or other v4 agents (SP CharpyCool is in materials_and_nanotechnology). Research constraint: the Tavily quota was exhausted and the shared WebSearch budget for the run was already used up, so machines were found by navigating manufacturers' own sites and sitemaps and reading their pages/PDFs directly; categories with no reachable full specification (LN2 cryogenic-machining delivery systems, cryogenic valve test rigs, industrial cryogenic grinding lines, LN2 shrink-fit baths) are not covered. Absences (magnet, sample vacuum, base pressure, window, sample wiring) are install=not_available only where a complete technical-data table defines the machine's scope; where no full spec is published (Cryogenics International) or a field source exists without a rating (SPEX electromagnetic impactor drive) the key is unknown and listed in not_found. Conventions: top-loading baths/chambers -> sample.diameter.max = smaller horizontal dimension, sample.height.max = depth; feed-size-limited mills -> both size keys = max feed size; Charpy tempering unit -> 10 mm cross-section, 55 mm length. Conservative choices: QualiBrittle NDA temperature.range recorded as -120..-70 C because the upper end is printed only as 'ambient'; NDA stability +/-2 C (LN2 range); DWTT uniformity +/-1 C recorded as 2 C gradient; SPEX sample mass 50 g (current page) not 100 g (old 6875 handbook); 'about' cooling/heating speeds and the 'about 60 L' DWTT tank volume not recorded. SPEX CG-400 and the Cryogenics International CI-1600 have only one documented process temperature (LN2 immersion at 77.34 K from NIST reference data; -196 C DCT soak), recorded as lo = hi.
